//detectors: One stop per evaluator in backend/checks.py EVALUATORS. Nothing here is invented: if a detector is not registered there it does not appear, and each stop's tone matches the status that evaluator would actually return for this specimen.

stops.label: The sheet
stops.title: One sheet. Nine detectors.
stops.body: A candidate verification sheet lands on the platen. Parakh reads it the way an examiner would — region by region — and every one of the nine checks below is a detector that actually ships.

stops.title: Is there a face, and can you see it?
stops.body: The affixed photograph is extracted as a raster region and scored on its own terms. Presence passes; absence is the finding.

stops.title: Signed, endorsed, sealed.
stops.body: Signature detection passes on presence and fails on absence — an unsigned sheet is the finding, not a guess at whose hand it was.

stops.title: Every code decoded, not just seen.
stops.body: The scan covers every page at the configured resolution and rotations. It passes on a decoded payload — spotting a code-shaped smudge is not the same as reading one.

stops.title: Can a machine read it at all?
stops.body: A battery of sub-tests scores whether the file is machine-readable. A sheet no tool can parse is a finding in its own right, long before anyone asks whether it is genuine.

stops.title: A glyph that does not belong.
stops.body: Every embedded typeface is enumerated and named. One glyph set that matches nothing else on the page is how a substituted grade gives itself away.

stops.title: The edit, localised.
stops.body: Compression residue, whitener traces and re-save generations are cross-read. The scan agrees with the font finding and puts the edit in one region rather than over the whole sheet.

stops.title: A photograph, or a photograph of a screen?
stops.body: Frequency analysis looks for the periodic pattern a screen or a reprint leaves behind. No anomalous peaks here — this is a first-generation capture.

stops.title: This one could not run — and says so.
stops.body: The same-phone test compares pages against each other to see whether one was captured on a different device. This sheet is a single page, so there is nothing to compare. It returns inconclusive with the reason, and is never quietly counted as a pass.

stops.title: Facts, deliberately without a verdict.
stops.body: How the file was generated: producer, creator, dates, re-save traces. Metadata never gets a tick or a cross and is excluded from every pass/fail total — a producer string is a fact about a file's origin, not a failure.

stops.title: Needs review — with the evidence attached.
stops.body: Parakh never decides for you. It hands back a verdict, the region it came from, and the reason in the detector's own words. The review stays human-led.
